reason: The text demonstrates this principle through contrasting examples of leadership. Moses exhibits responsibility by interceding on behalf of the people despite their rebellion, showing concern for their welfare and God's reputation. Caleb and Joshua similarly model accountability by taking responsibility to advocate for the people's best interests and encouraging faith, even at personal risk when the community threatens violence. Conversely, the ten spies who spread fear fail to take responsibility, demonstrating the negative consequences of absent accountability. The passage ultimately rewards Caleb and Joshua—those who maintained responsibility and faithfulness—by granting them entry to the promised land, implicitly endorsing their leadership model.
